failure_summary.description: Several calls were chosen from topical or keyword overlap rather than the operation and property actually requested.
Calls omitted or mis-mapped explicit constraints, or used values that did not match the endpoint's expected canonical form.
Some responses added unrelated or redundant calls while leaving a distinct requested outcome uncovered.
One response contained malformed JSON and could not be parsed.

patch.reasoning: Most endpoint-selection errors involved choosing by a shared word or broad topic instead of the requested meaning or data property. A focused clarification can help distinguish homonyms and ensure compound checks are matched to operations that explicitly return each property, without repeating the existing general call-set and schema audits.

edits.target: - Match the requested entity level and property as well as the topic: a result about a related component or sub-entity does not fulfill a request about the main entity, even when the search terms overlap.
edits.content: - Match the requested entity, operation, and property—not just shared topic words. Resolve ambiguous terms from their action and context before selecting a tool: a conceptual topic such as “faith” is not a same-named franchise. For compound checks, map each requested property to an endpoint whose own operation explicitly returns it; a disposable-status check does not establish deliverability or MX records unless that endpoint documents those results. A result about a related component or sub-entity does not fulfill a request about the main entity, even when the search terms overlap.
